request.description: Train the current PPO policy implementation from scratch under its existing 14-20 cm training exposure to create the first complete candidate for official-distribution measurement.
request.rationale: The physical model predicts that the decisive early distinction is official inner-radius coverage and sustained hold stability rather than nominal radial reachability. No candidate or development evidence exists yet. This baseline run supplies a concrete saved artifact; its training proxies will not be treated as performance evidence, and the candidate will be measured on the protected task-reference panel or an explicitly chosen official-distribution research panel with reach-versus-hold diagnostics.

request.description: Paired research evaluation of the two late PPO checkpoints on a shared 200-episode panel sampled from the official 6-20 cm radius and full angular distribution, preserving per-episode reach and hold diagnostics.
request.rationale: Training proxies plateau at 0.96 for checkpoints 115712 and 120832, but the training exposure omits official inner-radius targets and the terminal checkpoint has no privileged status. A same-seed comparison of these complete artifacts tests candidate capability under the relevant distribution and identifies whether failures are failure-to-reach or interruption of the required hold. Outcomes will determine which checkpoint, if either, is the credible working candidate and whether the next direction should target coverage, stabilization, or dynamics.

request.description: Analyze the paired M1 evaluation artifacts by official target-radius and angle strata, separating never-reached episodes from reached-but-failed-hold episodes and aggregating paired checkpoint wins by radius.
request.rationale: The M1 comparison establishes a large official-distribution gap but pooled success cannot determine whether the next intervention should expand inner-radius exposure, improve branch/transient control, or stabilize reached targets. This deterministic analysis consumes only the preserved M1 artifacts, validates their diagnostic consistency, and reports the requested strata without rerunning evaluation or introducing a candidate-selection proxy.

request.reason: M1 measured this complete candidate at 71.5% on a shared 200-episode research panel covering the official 6-20 cm radius, exceeding the preterminal checkpoint's 68.0%. M2 shows the gain is concentrated in the omitted inner regime, especially 10-14 cm (67.2% versus 57.4%), while outer performance is already 96.4-100%; this is currently the strongest evidence-backed artifact, though it remains far below the 98% objective.

request.candidates_and_roles: Best-known: T1:checkpoint-120832, assigned by E1 from M1 and M2. No working candidate is assigned. T1:checkpoint-115712 remains a measured comparison artifact, not a role assignment. No candidate meets the human goal, and no official assessment has been requested.
request.cumulative_resource_use: One fresh training operation T1 requested 120000 steps and produced checkpoints through 120832 because of the learning rollout boundary. One paired research evaluation M1 measured two complete checkpoints on 200 shared episodes each (400 policy-episode executions total). request.current_goal_gap: Best-known measured candidate T1:checkpoint-120832 achieved 71.5% (143/200) on M1, leaving 53 additional successes needed to reach the 196/200 objective on a comparable 200-episode panel. This is research evidence, not the protected official assessment. The main observed gap is concentrated at inner radii: M2 reports 32.7% for 6-10 cm and 67.2% for 10-14 cm, versus 96.4% and 100.0% for 14-18 cm and 18-20 cm.
request.current_synthesis: Established evidence: T1 trained the current PPO implementation under its existing 14-20 cm exposure; learning proxies reached 0.96 at checkpoints 115712 and 120832, but M1 measured only 68.0% and 71.5%, respectively, on the same 200-episode panel spanning the official 6-20 cm distribution. M2 validates that the terminal checkpoint's failures are predominantly never-reach failures (47 of 57), with 10 reached-but-failed-hold failures. Its radius-conditioned success is 32.7% at 6-10 cm, 67.2% at 10-14 cm, 96.4% at 14-18 cm, and 100.0% at 18-20 cm; angle-conditioned success is also asymmetric, ranging from 60.0% to 94.4%, but those pooled angle strata do not isolate a branch mechanism from radius. Interpretation: the sharp inner-radius transition supports the initial model's omitted-inner-regime and folded-posture/transient explanation as the leading direction. The low count of reached-but-failed-hold episodes means generic hold stabilization is not the first bottleneck for this artifact, although it remains consequential after coverage improves. The preterminal-versus-terminal gain is an artifact-level checkpoint comparison, not proof that additional steps caused the improvement. Unresolved alternatives include branch/shoulder-limit handling, singularity escape, and insufficient dynamic authority; M1/M2 contain no joint trajectories, actuator traces, contact traces, or causal intervention isolating these mechanisms. The evidence therefore supports changing exposure first, while limiting claims about the underlying controller mechanism.
request.decision_frontier: The consequential unresolved distinction is whether the 6-14 cm failure mass is primarily an exposure/generalization deficit that can be corrected by training on the official radius range, or whether it reflects a branch-aware transient/dynamic limitation that requires a controller or representation change. A discriminating next comparison is a fresh run with the official 6-20 cm target exposure and otherwise the current PPO implementation held fixed, measured against T1:checkpoint-120832 on the same official-distribution panel with the M2 radius/angle and failure-class diagnostics. If inner-radius never-reach failures fall substantially without sacrificing the already strong 14-20 cm behavior, exposure is the credible first intervention. If inner-radius failures persist or outer behavior degrades, the direction should shift toward branch/transient or dynamics-focused control investigation. Contact filtering, compiled inertial scale, and substep behavior remain unmeasured; they matter if the exposure comparison fails, but they do not need to be resolved before testing this direct, goal-relevant hypothesis.
request.human_goal_connection: The human objective requires at least 196 successes out of 200 under the official 6-20 cm, full-angle distribution with an uninterrupted 2-second hold. The first candidate achieves only 143/200 on an official-distribution research panel, so all scientific choices remain directed at closing that episode-success gap rather than optimizing training reward.

request.outcome: Negative bounded result for the tested artifact comparison: the fresh T2 candidate trained with official 6-20 cm exposure did not reduce 6-14 cm never-reach failures and substantially degraded outer-radius success relative to T1:checkpoint-120832. The result is a property of the compared complete artifacts and does not establish exposure causality or disprove broader exposure-based learning.

request.cumulative_resource_use: Before I1: one fresh T1 training request for 120,000 requested/120,832 completed steps; M1 evaluated two T1 checkpoints on 200 shared episodes each (400 policy-episode executions); M2 analyzed the paired M1 artifacts; E1 assigned best-known; E3 opened I1 and E4 checkpointed it. request.current_goal_gap: T1:checkpoint-120832 remains best-known but is far below the objective: 73.5% (147/200) on M3 and 71.5% (143/200) on M1. T2:checkpoint-120832, trained with the requested 6-20 cm exposure, achieved 35.0% (70/200) on M3. M4 shows T2 never reached in 120 episodes versus 42 for T1, with T2 success below T1 in every radius stratum, so the exposure comparison did not close the goal gap and did not produce a candidate for role assignment.
request.current_synthesis: Established observations: T1 used the current PPO implementation with 14-20 cm exposure and was measured at 71.5% on M1 and 73.5% on the fresh matched M3 panel; its failures were concentrated in the inner radii on M2/M4, but its 14-20 cm success was strong. T2 changed only the PI-owned training target-radius range to 6-20 cm, used a fresh PPO run with seed 1 and 120,832 completed steps, and retained the same PPO settings, shared scenario mechanics, reward, observations, action timing, and evaluation semantics. T2 was materially worse than T1 on M3: 35.0% versus 73.5%, paired delta -38.5 percentage points. M4 reports T2 never-reached=120 and reached-but-failed-hold=10 versus T1=42 and 11; T2 radius success was 22.8%, 24.6%, 44.4%, and 65.2% for 6-10, 10-14, 14-18, and 18-20 cm, while T1 was 31.6%, 75.4%, 100.0%, and 100.0%. Interpretation: the tested official-exposure artifact did not support continuing this exposure replacement and degraded both inner and outer behavior. Because training exposure and learned artifact/seed changed together, this is a property of the compared artifacts, not proof that official exposure alone is harmful or that broader exposure-based learning is disproven. The broad never-reach increase makes a transient, branch, initialization, or dynamic-authority explanation consequential, while the outer hold loss shows that complete-hold stabilization remains relevant. The angle asymmetry in M4 is a clue but not a branch diagnosis because the angle strata remain pooled across radius. Nominal point-kinematic reachability, compiled inertia and actuator authority, self-contact, and endpoint-versus-substep behavior remain unresolved; neither T2 nor M4 measured trajectories, torques, contacts, compiled fields, or substep distances.
request.decision_frontier: The unresolved consequential distinction is whether the new artifact's broad never-reach and angle/radius degradation reflects branch-aware transient and escape from the reset singularity, insufficient or poorly timed dynamic authority, or a training-optimization/artifact effect that cannot be attributed to exposure from this one fresh run. This distinction changes the next route toward 196/200: trajectory/control and compiled-dynamics evidence would justify mechanism-focused control or simulator investigation, whereas evidence of a reproducible learning/artifact effect would justify a redesigned training comparison. A useful discriminator must preserve complete-hold success while recording target geometry, q/qdot, branch errors, distance, action/effort, and preferably compiled inertial/actuator/contact or all-substep quantities at representative inner and outer targets. The present result does not warrant attributing failures to contact, dynamics, branches, or substep semantics; it only makes those alternatives more consequential after the exposure comparison failed.
request.human_goal_connection: The human goal remains at least 196 complete uninterrupted holds out of 200 under the official 6-20 cm full-angle distribution. The matched M3 panel measured the best-known T1 artifact at 147/200 (73.5%) and the fresh official-exposure T2 artifact at 70/200 (35.0%), so the campaign remains 49 successes short of the comparable 196/200 threshold on the latest baseline panel and is not ready for official assessment.
request.next_direction_or_closure: I1 is closed with a negative bounded conclusion. The tested official-exposure replacement did not improve the dominant 6-14 cm never-reach deficit and materially degraded outer-radius success, so the next goal review should choose between mechanism-focused diagnostics/intervention and a redesigned artifact-level learning comparison. The next question proposes trajectory and dynamics discrimination because M4 shows broad failure rather than an isolated inner-radius correction, but no mechanism is yet established and the campaign should not request official assessment.
